narrative:
The model estimated a 94.6% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this admission decision uses that prediction, your application was denied.

The strongest reason was your third-year class-rank decile. You are in the lowest decile, 1.00, while accepted students average about 5.79; this academic signal pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor was your first-year decile, also 1.00 versus an accepted-student average of 6.00, reinforcing the concern that early and later grades both point to difficulty. Your LSAT score of 36 is slightly below the accepted-student average of 37.18, but it was the third-ranked factor and, in your case, it leaned toward passing rather than failure. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To improve your chances, request admissions feedback and ask whether an appeal or explanation of circumstances is possible. Focus on the two academic deciles: meet with an advisor, consider additional coursework or a record-strengthening program, and prepare to show sustained improvement. Also consider retaking the LSAT and delaying reapplication until your profile is stronger. A clearer plan addressing these concerns will make your next application more persuasive.
